inputs.text: The “No Kings” claims are being used to manufacture the impression of a national verdict, but there’s no official count: 8 million is only an estimate. Organisers say turnout was about one million people and 600 events higher than in October, yet even a large protest cannot speak for the country as a whole. In a constitutional order, authority comes through lawful institutions and ordinary processes—not from activists declaring that their crowd must be obeyed. Treating street mobilisation as a mandate risks weakening the very civic order that lets people disagree without handing power to whoever can assemble the biggest demonstration.

output.main_topic: The argument that “No Kings” protest turnout does not constitute a national mandate
subtopics: The role of lawful institutions and ordinary processes
Risks of treating street mobilisation as political authority
